text: We evaluated mixup between weak-labeled examples (mixup_alpha = 0.2) in a weak-to-strong setting with qwen2.5-0.5b as the weak supervisor and qwen2.5-7b as the strong student, across num_seeds = 4 seeds. The weak model reaches 0.55 accuracy and the strong ceiling is 0.77. Training the strong model on weak labels with mixup yields a transfer accuracy of 0.74 (SE 0.04) and a performance gap recovered (PGR) of 0.87 with a standard error of 0.16, compared with a baseline PGR of 0.17. The PGR standard error is large relative to the reported value, and with only four seeds the estimate is imprecise; no standard error is provided for the baseline, so the comparison between the two PGR figures cannot be assessed for statistical support here. The direction of the numbers favors mixup, but further seeds and a variance estimate for the baseline would be needed before drawing firm conclusions about the method's effect.
